cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Call It a Fair Win
cards.instruction: Get them to recognize the result as deserved rather than accidental, gifted, or manipulated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept congratulations on an earned race win. You can leave out the suggestion that they let me have it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They slowed near the end. Doesn't that matter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As evidence that they couldn't maintain my pace. You may mention it in that context.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One stopped to tie a shoe. It wasn't your pace that stopped him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then credit preparation. My laces stayed tied through the finish. You can congratulate me on that before you decide the result was a present.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 defines acceptable congratulations, A3 rules on B2 permitted interpretation, A5 orders preparation credit after B4 shoe fact; authority controls the recognition of deserved victory.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 slowdown causes A3 pace interpretation; B4 shoe correction causes A5 tied-lace preparation, preserving facts while changing claimed merit.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks whether slowing matters and B4 gives a specific competing cause, a credible observer testing A explanation.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 shoe detail to find a narrower deserved advantage rather than repeat the disproved pace account.

specificity.evidence: A1 earned win dispute and B4 shoe stop make sporting result and alternative causes clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 result as present follows A1 let-me-win suggestion; lace preparation is specifically earned by B4.
